original.description: The User Management Service contract will encompass a comprehensive suite of offeringsdesigned to support and enhance user interactions and experience for ESA and Third PartyEO Missions.This service contract aims at integrating the User Communication and Information Portaltogether with the User Management functions, covered in the past by separate contracts,whereby ensuring autonomy to Industry in designing and using communication tools asadditional instrument to reach and stimulate a dynamic and variegated user community.The Information Portal is expected to provide seamless access to relevant content and data,Graphical and Editorial Servicesshall deliver visually engaging and professionally curatedmaterials, and finally User Experience Benchmarking Services enable performancecomparisons and insights. A dedicated User Help Desk completes the suite assisting userswith inquiries and technical support, ensuring prompt and effective resolution of issues.User Management Services will implement personalized access to tools, resources, andaccount features through the management of authorisation and authentication services withprovision of a secured User Area. The User Management service will foster a user-centricapproach that prioritizes accessibility, support, and continuous improvement driven by userfeedback.The User Management Service contract shall include the following services: Operations, maintenance and evolutions of the web services for data discoveryaccess and retrieval of Earth Observation products and information (composed byEarth Online, eoPortal, Swarm Data Handbook, EarthCARE Data Handbook, 3DVisuals and Quality Reports Advanced Search platforms). Content Management and Creation, including editorial and graphical services. Operations, maintenance and evolutions of an identity access management infrastructure with federated identity access configurations. Support to user community via a unique and integrated user help desk which serves as the single point of contact for answering to user enquiries and complaints, facilitating data access requests, monitoring and ensuring user satisfaction, and providing communications about system unavailability. The user help desk function will also provide AI powered chatbots and virtual support assistants being powered by a comprehensive and well-maintained and updated knowledgebase. Management of data access requests, assign authorisation to users for accessing restrained data, in agreement to applicable terms and condition (including quota management). Management of a large set of user profiles, including asecure and personalised self managementarea to access and manage account information, access settings and transaction history tracking support requests. By centralizing these functions, the userarea enhances convenience, engagement, and control, allowing users to efficiently interact with the system and AI powered virtual assistant while ensuring their dataand preferences are protected.  User experience benchmarking services for systematic analysing and monitoring of user and stakeholder feedback (surveys and behaviour analytics) and monitor performance to help identifying strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement

The initiative is being carried out in partnership with the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) and is funded by the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA) as part of the Global Gateway initiative.

original.description: Objective:To develop a portable modem that can be easily integrated in an existing optical ground station to make it compatible with ESTOL specificationsTargeted Improvements:Increased interoperability between existing optical ground stations and future satellite systems (e.g., HydRON).Description:There are a number of existing or planned optical ground stations (OGSs) that are currently used for scientific missions or to demonstrate quantum technologies. Those OGSs are not compliant to the ESA Specifications for Terabit/s Optical Links (ESTOL). To maximise the benefit of early Member State investments, the activity shall develop an upgrade kit" for multiple existing OGS infrastructures. An easy-to-integrate modem will facilitate the upgrade of such existing or planned OGSsand increase their interoperability with future commercial and institutional systems that will adopt ESTOL and its evolutions.Thisactivity shall develop a portable breadboard for an ESTOL-compliant modem. In the scope of the activity, it shall be assumed that thetarget existing OGSs have already been developed in terms of optical elements (e.g., aperture, adaptive optics, etc.) in order tobecompatible with ESTOL. The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. The functionalities of the portable modem shall be validated in the Contractor's laboratory and in an existing selected OGS.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: The objective of this activity is to design, implement and evaluate different types of satellite system architectural models aimed at dynamically focusing available resources on coverage gaps in terrestrial 4G and 5G networks.Targeted Improvements:Achieving national regulator coverage and service objectives for direct-to-device services and enabling twice as efficient satellite resourcespooling over the service area.Description: Today there are coverage gaps of the terrestrial telecommunication system despite initiatives from non-European industries to provide supplementary coverage from space. Concentrating satellite connectivity exclusively on coverage gap areas (including low service areas) rather than aiming for satellite connectivity over a broad coverage has the potential to maximize the efficiency of the satellite system. It could offer an increased throughput which translates in reduced deployment costs per bit and higher quality of service for end users. Moreover, this approach could enable flexible resources allocation based on the population density as well as step up and step down of terrestrial connectivity services.This activity will design,implement and evaluate satellite system architectural models addressing non-uniform spatiotemporal traffic patterns in particular of handheld services. First, the activity will develop a high-resolution spatiotemporal traffic model, which shall consider available datasets and trend analyses of service requirements of Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) and their representative organisations, along with actual and target service coverage obligation set by National Regulation Administrations (NRAs) for terrestrial network gaps. The outputs of this model will be used to define coverage gaps from existing and planned terrestrial networks and space networks. The activity will then study and implement in a software prototype Distributed Satellite System (DSS) concepts for Frequency Range 1 (FR1) considering different orbits, multi-connectivity techniques (e.g. beam overlapping, coordinated multi-point etc) and infrastructure configurations (e.g. fractionated, swarm and federated concepts). System sizing optimizing the satellite resources will be carried out of at least 3 selected DSS concepts and the performance will be evaluated by simulation. The activity shall identify the most promising DSS concept and development roadmap considering complexity and system performance and the ability to accommodateopportunities beyond direct to device services. original.description: ANUBIS (Asteroid NUdging By Ion-beam Shepherding) is a potential future Planetary Defence Cornerstone aiming to demonstrate the "ion beam shepherd" concept, which makes use of ion thrusters to deflect asteroids. The concept is of great interest to Planetary Defence and the scientific community, as demonstrated by various assessments, and in particular highlighted by the UN Space Mission Planning Advisory Group (SMPAG).
